source.snippet: In work we use LLMs exclusively. Nobody writes code anymore. It's all hands off and we have a high level understanding of how things work but no more than that. When it comes to my side project, I was adding features at breakneck speed with Claude but I realized I have no clue how the new code works or what it changes or breaks. I spent many years [building this app]... (2026-09-09)

problem_statement: Professional developers using LLMs to write code are losing comprehension of their own codebases — they ship fast but cannot explain, debug, or safely change what the AI wrote, creating hidden technical debt and fragility in production systems.
target_segment: Software developers and small engineering teams (2–20 engineers) at startups and SMBs who rely heavily on AI coding assistants (Claude, Copilot) in their daily workflow.
notes: Author has a production app with 'a solid user base' and is actively using Claude at work — clear professional buyer context. The pain is losing architectural understanding of code they ship, not just a learning complaint. Potential product angle: a tool that generates human-readable change summaries, dependency maps, or 'what did the AI actually do' audit trails after LLM-assisted coding sessions. Teams already paying for Copilot/Claude seats would be the natural buyers. Willingness-to-pay likely moderate-to-high given code quality and audit risk at work.
